record.original_question: For Minkowski's question mark function ?(x), define its Fourier-Stieltjes coefficients d_n by d_n = integral from 0 to 1 of cos(2 pi n x) d?(x). Does d_n tend to 0 as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: If real x = [0; a1 , ..., at , ...] ∈ [0, 1] is represented as a regular continued fraction with natural partial quotients, then Minkowski question mark function ?(x) is defined as follows
Here we would like to mention a famous open problem by R. Salem [130]: to prove or to disprove that for Fourier-Stieltjes coefficients dn , n ∈ N of ?(x) one has dn = ∫ cos(2πnx) d?(x) → 0, n → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let ?(x) denote Minkowski's question mark function on [0,1], defined as follows: for x = [0; a_1, a_2, a_3, ...] ∈ [0,1] written as a regular continued fraction with positive integer partial quotients a_i, set
  ?(x) = 2 · Σ_{k≥1} (-1)^{k+1} · 2^{-(a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_k)}.
The function ? is continuous and strictly increasing on [0,1], with ?(0)=0 and ?(1)=1, and it induces a Borel probability measure d? on [0,1] (singular with respect to Lebesgue measure). Define the Fourier–Stieltjes coefficients of ? by
  d_n = ∫_0^1 cos(2π n x) d?(x),   n ∈ ℕ.
Determine whether
  d_n → 0   as n → ∞.
artifact.category_tag: Minkowski question mark function / Salem's problem
artifact.status_search_result: Salem's 1943 problem on the decay of the Fourier–Stieltjes coefficients of Minkowski's question mark function has been resolved affirmatively. Yakubovich (2011, C. R. Math.) gave an affirmative answer using the Kontorovich–Lebedev transform, and Jordan and Sahlsten later established polynomial decay of the Fourier transform of the Minkowski measure, in particular implying d_n → 0.

status_evidence.title: The Fourier–Stieltjes transform of Minkowski's ?(x) function and an affirmative answer to Salem's problem

status_evidence.claim: The Fourier–Stieltjes coefficients of ?(x) vanish at infinity.
